rounds.text: Bajaj Auto Ltd is demonstrating exceptional fundamental momentum, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 25% [E17] and a profit growth of 27% [E21]. This top-tier operational execution is underpinned by stellar returns on capital, with ROE reaching 29.3% [E13] and ROCE hitting 38.5% [E12], significantly outperforming sector benchmarks such as a sector ROCE median of 13.8% [E77]. The business operates with extraordinary financial health, possessing a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x [E38] and generating robust free cash flow of Rs 8,470 Cr as of March 2026 [E36], supported by surplus cash reserves exceeding Rs 21,000 crores [E94]. Furthermore, capacity constraints—which management explicitly identified as a key constraint limiting sales by 10% to 15% [E90, E91, E97]—are being aggressively addressed through a planned 25% capacity expansion up to 9 million units per annum to fuel future growth [E84]. Demand tailwinds remain strong with domestic and international markets showing very positive sentiment [E81], and export volumes projected to push beyond 250,000 units per month [E100]. Conceded: the stock trades at an elevated valuation of 29x P/E [E1] and 9.06x price-to-book [E2], while institutional money flow currently reflects a negative signal [E44].

Bajaj Auto Ltd trades at a rich valuation that leaves little room for operational missteps, sitting at a P/E of 29 [E1] and a demanding price-to-book ratio of 9.06x [E2], which significantly outpaces the sector benchmark P/B of 5.75x [E7]. The company's recent price appreciation has outpaced fundamental profit growth, with a 5-year share price growth of 24% compared to 17% profit growth [E56], and short-term price growth exceeding profit growth by 13% [E57], signaling that expectations are running ahead of delivery. Furthermore, the stock sits at 99% of its 52-week range [E48] and only -0.3% away from its 52-week high [E49], reflecting an extended entry point where much of the good news is already discounted [E71]. Institutional confidence is showing cracks, highlighted by a negative institutional money flow signal [E44] and foreign institutional holding dropping from 14.37% in Sep 2023 to 9.01% in Jun 2026 [E42]. Compounding these valuation and sentiment risks, the business faces near-term operational headwinds, including intensive commodity inflation hitting 4.5% of revenue [E87] and supply chain, logistics, and ransomware disruptions that impaired availability by 10% to 15% [E96, E97]. Conceded: [E36], [E60].

Conceded: [E1], [E2], [E42], [E48], [E49], [E56], [E57]. While the bear flags a high price-to-book ratio [E2] and an extended price near its 52-week high [E48], these metrics ignore the fundamental engine driving the stock: an extraordinary return on capital employed of 38.5% [E12] and an ROE of 29.3% [E13] that vastly outperform sector benchmarks [E10]. The alleged mismatch between price and profit growth [E56, E57] is entirely justified by a top-tier quantitative rules-based screen scoring 94 out of 100 [E64], propelled by a 25% surge in trailing sales growth [E17] and a 27% leap in profit growth [E21]. Furthermore, pointing to foreign institutional holding drops [E42] misses the offsetting confidence from domestic institutions, whose holdings grew from 9.03% to 13.42% [E43]. Finally, the operational disruptions cited by the bear [E96, E97] stem not from structural failure, but from overwhelming demand; capacity constraints are so severe that management is actively expanding capacity by 25% to reach 9 million units per annum [E84] to capture robust, positive demand across domestic and international markets [E81].

Conceded: [E12], [E13], [E17], [E21], [E64], [E81], [E84]. The bull attempts to minimize the high valuation by pointing to strong profitability [E12, E13], yet ignores that the stock trades at an expensive P/B ratio of 9.06x [E2] compared to a sector benchmark of 5.75x [E7]. While the bull celebrates surging sales and profit metrics [E17, E21], it overlooks the fact that price growth has outpaced profit growth [E56, E57], signaling that expectations are already running ahead of fundamental delivery. The bull dismisses the institutional outflow [E42] by highlighting domestic buying [E43], but the overall signal engine still registers a negative money flow with institutional holdings dropping by 0.74 percentage points [E44]. Finally, attributing operational issues solely to overwhelming demand ignores management's own admissions that supply chain difficulties, logistics disruptions, and a ransomware attack forced production suspensions and impaired service availability by 10% to 15% [E96, E97].

Conceded: [E2]. While the price-to-book ratio is elevated [E2, E7], it is fully justified by elite returns on capital: ROA reaches 14.96% versus a sector benchmark of 1.55% [E8], ROCE hits 24.52% compared to the sector's 14.72% [E10], and overall ROCE stands at a staggering 38.5% [E12]. The bear's concern over price growth outpacing profit growth [E56, E57] ignores that this premium valuation is fueled by outstanding operational acceleration, including a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 25% [E17] and profit growth of 27% [E21]. Furthermore, pointing to negative money flow [E44] and institutional outflows [E42] misses the crucial reality that domestic institutions have aggressively stepped in, increasing their stake from 9.03% to 13.42% [E43]. Finally, while supply chain disruptions and a ransomware attack temporarily impacted availability by 10% to 15% [E96, E97], management successfully defended against these headwinds [E96], turning constraints into a clear signal of overwhelming demand that has prompted a 25% capacity expansion up to 9 million units per annum [E84].

Conceded: [E8], [E10], [E12]. While those capital return figures are high, the bull completely glosses over the severe valuation penalties that accompany them, specifically a price-to-book ratio of 9.06x against a sector benchmark of 5.75x [E2, E7] and an explicit insider warning that the stock is trading at a rich valuation where the price already discounts a lot of the good news [E71]. The bull's dismissal of the price-growth-outpacing-profit-growth signal is unpersuasive when the evidence explicitly flags that expectations are running ahead of delivery and the stock sits 99% of the way up its 52-week range [E48, E57, E72]. Conceded: [E43]. Although domestic institutions increased their stake to 13.42%, this fails to offset the broader institutional money flow reading as negative [E44] alongside a steep drop in foreign institutional ownership from 14.37% down to 9.01% [E42]. Finally, framing temporary supply chain constraints, logistical disruptions, and a ransomware attack that suspended operations simply as a sign of overwhelming demand [E96, E97, E98] downplays real operational risks that impaired service availability by up to 15% [E97].

evidence.quote: This is bound to slow down the motorcycle category from its rocking 20% growth in Q4 to we estimate 7% to 9% in the near term.

evidence.fact: The company expects its export volume to move to 2,20,000-plus units per month in the current quarter.
evidence.quote: We are looking at moving the exports needle to 2,20,000 units per month this quarter, up from the 2,00,000 levels.

evidence.fact: Material cost inflation is estimated to be approximately 3.5% to 4% of revenue.
evidence.quote: Taken together, we are currently estimating a material cost inflation impact of approximately 3.5% to 4% of revenue.

evidence.fact: Management stated that the demand environment across both domestic and international key markets is very positive.
evidence.quote: Having said that, the demand environment, both in domestic and international, particularly in our key markets, is very positive, though the business environment may still be a bit volatile.

evidence.fact: The domestic motorcycle industry had a split trajectory in FY26, featuring a muted first half followed by a strong second half.
evidence.quote: Domestic motorcycles, the industry had a split trajectory in FY '26 with a muted first half, followed by a strong recovery in the second half.

evidence.fact: The demand environment softened in April due to general inflation, increased vehicle prices, LPG shortages, and manpower migration.
evidence.quote: The demand environment, it has softened in April due to general inflation, increased prices of our vehicles, LPG shortages, manpower migration and the LPG shortage-led effect on the consumer sentiment.

evidence.fact: The company is undertaking an expansion of capacity by almost 25% from the current 7 million units per annum to 9 million units per annum.
evidence.quote: So, with an eye on the future, we are undertaking an expansion of capacity by almost 25% from the current 7 million units per annum across different businesses to progressively go up to 9 million units per annum.

evidence.fact: Key areas for capacity expansion will include electric vehicles for two-wheelers and three-wheelers, high-end motorcycles, and three-wheelers.
evidence.quote: The key areas to address will be EVs, both two-wheelers and three-wheelers, high-end motorcycles and three-wheelers.

evidence.fact: Manufacturing capacity in Brazil has increased to 60,000 units per annum.
evidence.quote: Sales nearly 10,000 units during the quarter, supported by expanded manufacturing capacity, which has now increased to 60,000 units per annum, successful new product introductions like the 400 NS and wider market presence with almost 70 top-class stores.

evidence.fact: Commodity inflation intensified during the quarter, taking the overall impact to about 4.5% of revenue.
evidence.quote: Through the quarter, commodity inflation intensified even further. Inflation across the metals complex accelerated meaningfully through May, taking the overall inflationary impact for the quarter to about 4.5% of revenue.

evidence.fact: Calibrated pricing actions implemented through April and June enabled the company to offset nearly about half of the inflation.
evidence.quote: That said, we also responded decisively. And as I had indicated in the previous call, we responded with calibrated pricing very judiciously taken through April and June, enabling us to offset nearly about half of the inflation through pricing.

evidence.fact: EBITDA margins inched up to 20.9%, representing a sequential improvement of 10 basis points.
evidence.quote: EBITDA margins inched up to 20.9%, an improvement of 10 basis points sequentially despite the hyperinflationary commodity environment that I'd spoken about.

evidence.fact: Capacity issues restricted sales of some models both in India and overseas.
evidence.quote: Capacity issues restricted sales of some models, both in India and overseas.

evidence.fact: Capacities have emerged as a key constraint to growth for the business.
evidence.quote: Capacities have emerged as a key constraint to growth.

evidence.fact: Total volumes for Q4 reached a new high of 13.7 lakh units, growing 24% year-on-year.
evidence.quote: Total volumes reached a new high of 13.7 lakh units, growing 24% year-on-year.

evidence.fact: The company generated over INR 2,300 crores of free cash flow during the quarter, achieving a cash conversion of nearly 80% of profit after tax.
evidence.quote: We generated over INR2,300 crores of free cash flow during this quarter, almost double that of the same period last year, translating into a cash conversion of almost 80% of profit after tax.

evidence.fact: The balance sheet remains healthy with surplus cash in excess of INR 21,000 crores at the end of the June quarter.
evidence.quote: The balance sheet continues to remain very healthy with surplus cash in excess of INR21,000 crores at the end of the June quarter, well managed and providing sufficient fuel for future growth investments, strategic opportunities and improved shareholder returns.

evidence.fact: Surplus funds closed the year at over INR18,000 crores after deploying capital on multiple fronts.
evidence.quote: We closed the year with surplus funds of over INR18,000 crores after deploying capital on multiple fronts during the year, reflecting a strong and consistent cash generation.

evidence.fact: Operations were suspended for a few days due to a ransomware attack while exercising abundant caution.
evidence.quote: It was a tough quarter with RM inflation, supply chain and logistics disruptions as well as a ransomware attack, which you may have read about, but it was defended comprehensively and successfully. Though exercising abundant caution, we suspended operations for a few days to complete thorough checks and investigations.

evidence.fact: Disruptions impaired availabilities by about 10% to 15%, particularly affecting exports, high-end bikes, and EVs.
evidence.quote: All of these above issues combined impaired availabilities by about 10% to 15%, more so in exports, high-end bikes and EVs.

evidence.fact: Supply chain difficulties regarding LPG shortages, manpower availability, and outbound logistics impaired service availability by about 10% to 15%.
evidence.quote: Supply chain difficulties in terms of the LPG shortage, manpower availability and outbound logistics to overseas markets have impaired availability to service demand by about 10% to 15%.

evidence.fact: Management commitment: The company aims to accomplish an exhaustive portfolio makeover in the 125cc segment within the next 6 weeks.
evidence.quote: Our aim is to accomplish this exhaustive portfolio makeover within the next 6 weeks.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (this quarter): The export business is looking at moving exports beyond the 250,000 per month level this quarter and onwards.
evidence.quote: Overall, the exports business, which like I said is 40% of our revenue, has established an outstanding growth momentum and we are looking at moving exports to beyond the 2,50,000 per month level this quarter and onwards.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (next 2 years): New product ranges in both the 125cc and 150cc plus segments will hit the market starting in July under the Pulsar brand.
evidence.quote: There will be hopefully, I think we will see these new introductions hitting the market as early as July in the Pulsar brand itself.
